title: The Fields Where Every Building Knows What It Owes

features.name: the bookkeeping shed
features.desc-on-touch: A small structure with windows you cannot see through. Inside, the architecture keeps its own accounts, calculating what it owes the ground, the sky, the rain that falls on its roof.

features.name: the ledger fields
features.desc-on-touch: Rows of measurement stakes dividing the horizon into parcels of what is owed. Each stake marks a debt that has learned to grow roots.

features.name: the tallied tower
features.desc-on-touch: A structure that rises in exact increments, each level recording what was added to the sum. It stops growing when it reaches the amount owed.

features.name: the calculation ground
features.desc-on-touch: Where you walk, the dust beneath your feet holds the weight of figures. The horizon has learned to weigh what stands upon it.

features.name: the numbered shelter
features.desc-on-touch: Another building, marked with sequential plaques. Inside, the rooms are sized according to debts measured in increments of loss.

inscription: every stone here keeps tally, and the horizon is the accountant that learned to love numbers more than forgetting

file.name: Ledger_Of_Structural_Obligation.txt
file.note: A building register where each entry is written in a hand that grows increasingly precise, ending in perfect accounting script that resembles mathematics more than language

exits.label: back down to where things still owed but could not count
westward where the debt horizon finally admits zero
eastward into further horizons that calculate
